candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is septic arthritis, an infectious etiology. C001 attributes the bilateral knee arthritis to methotrexate toxicity/reaction, which is a different causal mechanism and diagnostic category. While methotrexate can cause joint symptoms, the clinical picture—bilateral knee effusions with synovial thickening, markedly elevated ESR (100 mm/h) and CRP (43 mg/L), leukocytosis (WBC 13,600), and thrombocytosis (576,000)—is more consistent with an infectious process. The candidate asserts an incompatible etiology (drug-induced vs. septic/infectious), making it a conflicting subtype rather than a partial or equivalent match.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Drug-induced rheumatologic reaction versus infectious joint process

case_quality_flags: No joint aspiration/culture results documented; septic arthritis diagnosis rests on clinical and imaging grounds without microbiologic confirmation
Bilateral symmetric joint involvement is atypical for classic septic arthritis; gonococcal or reactive arthritis could also be considered, but reference diagnosis is septic arthritis
